doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Self-promotion, quartet and word of mouth
summary: His website, a Bechet and Spanier tribute quartet, and how Riverwalk reruns and records bring work.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Do you do a certain amount of your own promotion to try to keep your name — I mean even like a place like this — do you try to make sure that the promoter doesn’t forget about you or is it not necessary? Do you think you’re in the circuit enough that —

Yeah I think so. I do a certain amount of promotion personally on certain things. Like I have a website, a web page, and I have a little quartet group that Phil Flanigan plays with, we were talking about Phil before, and a couple of guys from Florida. We try to do tributes to the things that Sidney Bechet and Muggsy Spanier did in the 40s, with just guitar and bass and cornet and clarinet. And we have been trying to promote that some more to get some more work for it, but other than that, the rest of it, a lot of this business is through word of mouth and through recordings. People hear your records and they say oh gee, this is a good guy, let’s get this guy, and that’s kind of the way it works. So I would say the things that have helped me promotionally-wise within the last five years has been the Riverwalk radio show, because they still do a lot of re-runs and I’m on the show still quite a bit. They do compilation shows too, so I may have recorded a whole show and now I’ll listen to it and I’ll hear myself for like two tunes and then somebody else. Plus, and the record label, because since I’ve done a lot of recording for them in the last five years. I’ve got about oh I’d say six or seven CDs out so far in the last five years. Maybe even a little bit more than that. Because I’ve also done some things as sideman for other guys.
These parties here are almost like you have your own little fan club sometimes. I see all the people come up, and, “I saw you in Sarasota” and, “would you sign this.” It’s a nice situation.

Yeah that’s what happens. It’s nice, and you do run across some of the same people.
